newsitem.title: GERMANY: Second tranche of new German 10-yr yields 5.87 pct.
newsitem.headline: Second tranche of new German 10-yr yields 5.87 pct.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Tuesday that the 5.502 billion marks worth of a new 10-year bond with a 6.0 percent coupon issued by the German government had been allocated to the market in an auction.
The central bank, which acts as issuing agent, said the paper had been alloted at prices of 100.88 and above. The average price was 100.91 and the average yield 5.87 percent.

The allocation brings the total value of the issue up to 15 billion marks. Five billion marks of the bond to the Federal Bond Consortium in a first tranche on Tuesday and a further 4.498 billion is being held for price-smoothing activities.
The Bundesbank said the new 10-year would come due on July 4, 2007 -- a maturity of 10 years and 69 days.
The first yield interest rate payment will be made on July 4, 1998 for 429 interest-earning days, it said.
The series number for the new bond is WKN 133 503.
